chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjal, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, from Isma'il ibn Jabir or 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:
I said to Abī 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Indeed, I rise in the latter part of the night and fear the coming of dawn. So he said: Recite al-Hamd and hasten, hasten.

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: the latter part of the night, the time near dawn
key_terms.اعْجَلْ: hasten or perform it quickly due to limited time
key_terms.اقْرَأِ الْحَمْدَ: recite Surat al-Hamd, meaning al-Fatihah in the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat al-layl if they fear dawn is about to break?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning one who performs salat in the latter part of the night and fears the arrival of dawn. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs such a person to suffice with reciting al-Hamd and to hasten, indicating facilitation in the time-sensitive performance of the night prayer.
